description: ECDAT Cryptographic Algorithm and Protocol Risk Assessment Rules

algorithms.deprecation_notes: MD5 is completely broken classically due to practical collision attacks (RFC 6151). Collision generation takes seconds.
algorithms.remediation_hint: Migrate immediately to SHA-256 or SHA-3/BLAKE3 for general hashing; Argon2id for password hashing.

algorithms.deprecation_notes: SHA-1 has proven practical collision attacks (SHAttered, Shambles). Forbidden for digital signatures and certificates by NIST since Dec 2022.
algorithms.remediation_hint: Upgrade to SHA-256, SHA-384, or SHA-3. For HMAC, SHA-1 is not broken by collisions but should be phased out.

algorithms.deprecation_notes: SHA-224 provides 112 bits of classical collision resistance. Being phased out in favor of SHA-256+.
algorithms.remediation_hint: Adopt standard SHA-256 for broader interoperability and 128-bit security level.

algorithms.deprecation_notes: Standard secure hash algorithm providing 128-bit collision resistance and 256-bit preimage resistance against classical attackers. Grover search reduces preimage to 128 bits, which remains secure.
algorithms.remediation_hint: Compliant and secure for general applications.

algorithms.deprecation_notes: Standard high-security hash algorithm providing 192-bit classical collision resistance. Recommended for CNSA Suite and Top Secret data.
algorithms.remediation_hint: Secure and recommended for high-security applications.

algorithms.deprecation_notes: Standard high-security hash algorithm providing 256-bit collision resistance and 512-bit preimage resistance.
algorithms.remediation_hint: Secure and recommended for high-performance 64-bit architectures.

algorithms.deprecation_notes: Sponge-construction hash function resistant to length-extension attacks. Provides strong quantum security margin against Grover's algorithm.
algorithms.remediation_hint: State-of-the-art secure hash standard.

conditions.note: RSA keys under 2048 bits are factorable or insecure against modern compute.
2048-bit RSA provides 112-bit classical security; disallowed by NIST after 2030.
3072-bit and 4096-bit RSA provide 128-bit classical security, but completely vulnerable to Shor's algorithm on a CRQC.

algorithms.deprecation_notes: All RSA variants are fully broken by Shor's algorithm on a Cryptographically Relevant Quantum Computer (CRQC), which factors integers in polynomial time.
algorithms.remediation_hint: Plan migration to ML-KEM (FIPS 203) for key encapsulation and ML-DSA / SLH-DSA (FIPS 204/205) for signatures. Use hybrid schemes (e.g. X25519+ML-KEM-768) during transition.

algorithms.deprecation_notes: DSA is deprecated in FIPS 186-5 for digital signature generation. Fragile to nonce reuse and broken by Shor's algorithm.
algorithms.remediation_hint: Migrate to Ed25519 classically or ML-DSA (FIPS 204) for post-quantum security.

conditions.note: Curves smaller than 256 bits have inadequate classical security.
Classically secure, but completely broken by Shor's algorithm on a CRQC.

algorithms.deprecation_notes: Elliptic Curve Discrete Logarithm Problem (ECDLP) is solved in polynomial time by Shor's algorithm. All NIST and SECG curves will be broken by a CRQC.
algorithms.remediation_hint: Migrate to ML-DSA (FIPS 204) or stateful hash signatures (LMS/XMSS) for firmware. Use dual-signature hybrid schemes in interim.

algorithms.deprecation_notes: Classically sound with curves >= 256 bits, but vulnerable to Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later (HNDL) attacks because recorded key exchanges can be retroactively broken by Shor's algorithm.
algorithms.remediation_hint: Adopt hybrid key exchange combining X25519 or P-256 with ML-KEM-768 (X25519MLKEM768).

conditions.note: Logjam attack showed 1024-bit DH can be broken by nation-state classical compute.
Classically acceptable, but broken by Shor's algorithm on a CRQC.

algorithms.deprecation_notes: Finite-field DH is computationally expensive, prone to small-subgroup attacks, and completely broken by Shor's algorithm.
algorithms.remediation_hint: Replace with ECDH (X25519) combined with ML-KEM-768.

algorithms.deprecation_notes: Gold-standard classical ECDH key exchange offering 128-bit security, high performance, and side-channel resistance. Vulnerable to Shor's algorithm on a CRQC.
algorithms.remediation_hint: Combine with ML-KEM-768 in hybrid mode (X25519MLKEM768) to protect against Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later.

conditions.note: AES-128 provides 128-bit classical security. Grover's algorithm provides a quadratic speedup, reducing effective security to 64 bits against an optimal quantum exhaustive search.
AES-256 provides 256-bit classical security and 128-bit quantum security against Grover's algorithm, satisfying all post-quantum security levels.

algorithms.deprecation_notes: AES is NOT broken by quantum computers. Grover's algorithm halves key length search complexity (O(2^(n/2))), meaning AES-256 retains 128 bits of quantum security margin.
algorithms.remediation_hint: For long-lived confidential data (shelf-life > 10 years), upgrade from AES-128 to AES-256 in authenticated modes (GCM, GCM-SIV). Ensure GCM nonces are never reused.

algorithms.deprecation_notes: Single DES has a 56-bit key which can be brute-forced in hours classically (RFC 4772). Formally withdrawn by NIST.
algorithms.remediation_hint: Immediately replace with AES-256-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305.

algorithms.deprecation_notes: Sweet32 attack (CVE-2016-2183) exploits 64-bit block size collision vulnerability. Disallowed in TLS and deprecated by NIST after 2023.
algorithms.remediation_hint: Replace with AES-GCM (128 or 256-bit).

algorithms.deprecation_notes: Vulnerable to related-key attacks and typically deployed with weak 40-bit export keys.
algorithms.remediation_hint: Replace with AES-256-GCM.

algorithms.deprecation_notes: RC4 contains profound statistical biases in keystream (Bar Mitzvah, RC4 NOMORE attacks). Prohibited in TLS by RFC 7465.
algorithms.remediation_hint: Prohibit all RC4 usage immediately; replace with AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305.

algorithms.deprecation_notes: High-performance authenticated cipher resistant to cache-timing attacks. 256-bit key provides 128 bits of security against Grover search.
algorithms.remediation_hint: Excellent secure cipher for mobile and embedded platforms without hardware AES acceleration.

algorithms.deprecation_notes: Formally deprecated by IETF in RFC 8996. Vulnerable to BEAST, POODLE, CBC-padding oracle attacks, and weak MD5/SHA-1 signatures.
algorithms.remediation_hint: Disable TLS 1.0 across all servers and clients; require TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3.

algorithms.deprecation_notes: Formally deprecated by IETF in RFC 8996. Relies on SHA-1 handshakes and lacks modern AEAD-only ciphersuites.
algorithms.remediation_hint: Disable TLS 1.1 across all configurations; require TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3.

conditions.condition: TLS 1.2 with static RSA or CBC ciphers
conditions.note: Static RSA lacks Forward Secrecy; CBC mode vulnerable to Lucky13 timing attacks.
Classically secure with AEAD ciphers and Ephemeral Diffie-Hellman.

algorithms.deprecation_notes: TLS 1.2 supports legacy insecure cipher suites and relies on classical key exchange (ECDHE/DHE) vulnerable to Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later.
algorithms.remediation_hint: Mandate AEAD ciphersuites only. Enable TLS 1.3 with hybrid post-quantum key exchange.

algorithms.deprecation_notes: Current state-of-the-art TLS protocol. Eliminates legacy insecure ciphers and mandates forward secrecy. Classical key exchange remains vulnerable to CRQC without hybrid PQC groups.
algorithms.remediation_hint: Configure TLS 1.3 with hybrid post-quantum key exchange groups (X25519MLKEM768 or SecP256r1MLKEM768).
